# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 (Bi-Vb Pc16)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc16
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 16. Sitting down without permission

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 16 (*Anāpucchāabhinisīdana*) is an expiation rule governing the monastic decorum of Buddhist nuns when visiting lay households [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a nun who sits down or lies down on a seat in a house without first obtaining permission from the residents commits an offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that the rule addresses instances where a nun displays undue familiarity within a lay family and disregards the courtesy and etiquette expected of a guest [Hüsken 1997].

Textually and conceptually, Pācittiya 16 forms a tight thematic cluster with the preceding rule (Pācittiya 15) and the following rule (Pācittiya 17) [Hüsken 1997]. While Pācittiya 15 deals with leaving after having sat down on a seat (*āsane nisīditvā pakkameyya*), Pācittiya 16 varies this phrasing slightly by prohibiting sitting down or lying down on a seat (*āsane abhinisīdeyya vā abhinipajjeyya vā*) without prior authorization [Hüsken 1997]. This close textual affinity is reflected in DharmaNexus data, which identifies extensive internal text reuse across the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, with the largest shared textual passages occurring with Pācittiya 17 (e.g., §2.1.15–2.3.8 ↔ §2.1.19–2.3.7) and Pācittiya 15 (e.g., §1.9–2.3.8 ↔ §1.12–2.3.8), alongside matches in other pācittiya rules such as Bi-Vb Pc94 and Pc80 [DharmaNexus].

The rule has direct counterparts in the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Pc 16) and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Pc 16) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also records widespread parallels across other early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, including the Dharmaguptaka (e.g., Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 84), Mahīśāsaka (e.g., Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 129), Mahāsāṅghika (e.g., Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 85), Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc85*), Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions in Chinese and Tibetan translations [SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus aligns passages of this rule with Sanskrit fragments of the *Prātimokṣasūtra* and *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation is provided on SuttaCentral by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
